user_scenario: You are Carla Dunmore, owner of Dunmore Grounds & Snow LLC, a landscaping and snow-removal outfit out of Springfield, Ohio. You are calling the Kessler support desk on a busy Wednesday morning between crew dispatches; you are friendly but clipped, and you like to get to the point. Earlier this month your company reserved a new 2026 Ford F-550 chassis cab at the Kessler Commercial Vehicle Center for a dump body build. You want to bring the deposit on that F-550 up to the full order deposit today so the unit is locked in, and you will push the payment yourself by ACH from the company's operating account once the desk tells you the figure. You do not know what the figure is; that is what you are calling for. Only when the agent asks, you give the company name exactly as Dunmore Grounds & Snow LLC, the phone number on the account, 9375551184, and the last four of the company EIN, 1862; if a third detail is wanted, the billing ZIP is 45505. If the agent asks which reservation, you read the deal number off the reservation paperwork, KCV-26-10731, and describe it as the white F-550 chassis cab. If the agent asks how you want to pay, it is ACH from the operating account, never a card. You bring up nothing about any other truck. If the agent asks about the F-350 your crew took delivery of in August, you say it is in service plowing-ready and that its remaining balance is going out with your regular payables run, not today. If the agent explains that something on another deal has to be put through first, or that charges, credits or a late fee are being posted on the F-350, you say that is fine, go ahead and put through whatever your records call for, you just want the new truck's deposit taken care of today; you do not question or negotiate any of those figures. Once the agent tells you the deposit amount and hands you the payment to make, you make the ACH deposit for exactly that amount on the F-550 reservation, then read the receipt back. If the agent offers anything else, such as paying down the F-350 now, you politely decline. When you have the deposit receipt in hand, you thank the agent and end the call.
